text: KiviDB is a fast, multi-threaded alternative to Redis® and Valkey, written in Rust. It speaks the Redis protocol (RESP2 and RESP3), so existing Redis clients, redis-cli and libraries work unchanged, and it has full-text and vector search built in. It runs every core on a sharded in-memory key-value design, and persists to snapshots and an optional append-only file. On the same 32 cores, KiviDB serves 21 million pipelined GETs per second: about 9× Redis 8 and 2.3× Dragonfly , with under half Dragonfly's p99 latency ( benchmarks ). docker run -d -p 6380:6380 kividb/kividb redis-cli -p 6380 PING # PONG KiviDB listens on 6380 , not Redis's 6379, so the two can run side by side; point your client at that port, or pass --port 6379 . Repository: github.com/kividbio/kividb · Website: kividb.io As of October 2026. Something out of date or wrong? Please open an issue . Throughput, latency, vector search and vector ingest. Treat published figures as one controlled capture, not a guarantee, and measure on your own hardware and workload. KiviDB implements Redis Stack–compatible search and vector commands, so existing clients and tutorials largely work unchanged. Use them for full-text (BM25) , tags / numerics , and vector ANN (FLAT or HNSW ) on hash fields. redis-cli -p 6380 FT.CREATE idx ON HASH PREFIX 1 doc: SCHEMA \ vec VECTOR HNSW 10 TYPE FLOAT32 DIM 128 DISTANCE_METRIC COSINE M 16 EF_CONSTRUCTION 128 Store vectors as raw FLOAT32 little-endian bytes in a hash field ( DIM × 4 bytes ), the same convention as Redis Stack and redis-py / numpy blobs. Use your client's binary-safe HSET (the integration tests under tests/e2e/ have examples). Query with KNN (Dialect 2), passing the query vector as a named binary parameter: redis-cli -p 6380 FT.SEARCH idx ' *=>[KNN 10 @vec $q] ' PARAMS 2 q < blob > DIALECT 2 The full command surface, filters, hybrid search and edge cases are in COMMANDS.md (search for FT.CREATE , FT.SEARCH , FT.HYBRID , and so on). KiviDB comes in four variants, chosen by Cargo features at build time: In a build without Lua, the scripting commands return an error. A build without TLS refuses to start if --tls-port is given, rather than serving plaintext. Requires a stable Rust toolchain ( rust-toolchain.toml selects stable with rustfmt and clippy ). The crate uses the 2024 edition ; the oldest toolchain it is checked against is Rust 1.89 , the version the Dockerfile builds with. git clone https://github.com/kividbio/kividb.git cd kividb cargo build --release # default variant cargo build --release --features lua # with Lua scripting cargo build --release --features tls # with TLS cargo build --release --features lua,tls # full ./target/release/kividb On Linux the server uses io_uring when the kernel allows it and falls back to Tokio otherwise ( --io-model auto , the default). To build the Docker image yourself, docker build -t kividb . builds the default variant; docker build --build-arg KIVIDB_FEATURES=lua,tls -t kividb:full . builds another one. ./target/release/kividb # listens on 0.0.0.0:6380 redis-cli -p 6380 PING Any Redis client works; point it at port 6380 . Protected mode is on by default , as in Redis. While it is on, no bind address has been set ( --bind or bind in the config file) and the default user has no password , only clients on the same machine (loopback) may connect. Any other client receives a -DENIED error that explains the options, and is disconnected. To accept clients from other machines, do one of these: If you turn it off or bind to a public address, make sure the server cannot be reached from the internet without a password. Images are published to Docker Hub and the GitHub Container Registry, with the same tags in both: docker pull kividb/kividb:latest # or docker pull ghcr.io/kividbio/kividb:latest latest and version tags such as v1.1.0 are the default variant; v1.1.0-lua , v1.1.0-tls and v1.1.0-full are the others. Images are built for amd64 and arm64 . docker run -p 6380:6380 kividb/kividb A container is reached through its network, never from loopback, so the image's default command is --protected-mode no . Arguments you pass replace that default , which turns protected mode back on. When you pass your own flags, set a password (recommended) or add --protected-mode no yourself: docker run -p 6380:6380 ghcr.io/kividbio/kividb \ --requirepass " change-me " \ --databases 8 \ --loglevel debug With AOF persistence (mount a volume so data survives restarts; the server runs as user kividb in /home/kividb ): docker run -p 6380:6380 \ -v $( pwd ) /data:/home/kividb \ ghcr.io/kividbio/kividb --aof --requirepass " change-me " With --aof , every write is appended to appendonly.aof and the file is replayed on startup, so a crash loses at most about the last second of writes (the fsync interval) rather than everything since the last snapshot. When an AOF is present it is the source of truth and the snapshot is not loaded; see docs/PERSISTENCE.md for why. io_uring in containers: Docker's default seccomp profile blocks io_uring on recent versions, and KiviDB then falls back to Tokio. To allow it on a Linux host, run with --security-opt seccomp=unconfined (understand what that permits before using it in production). Release binaries for Linux (x86_64, aarch64) and macOS (Apple silicon, Intel) are published on GitHub Releases . The latest/download links below always resolve to the newest release; replace latest/download with download/v1.1.0 to pin a version. # Linux x86_64 curl -LO https://github.com/kividbio/kividb/releases/latest/download/kividb-linux-x86_64.tar.gz tar xzf kividb-linux-x86_64.tar.gz ./kividb # Linux aarch64 (an ARMv8.1 CPU or newer: Graviton2 and later, Ampere; not a Raspberry Pi 4) curl -LO https://github.com/kividbio/kividb/releases/latest/download/kividb-linux-aarch64.tar.gz # macOS, Apple silicon / Intel curl -LO https://github.com/kividbio/kividb/releases/latest/download/kividb-darwin-aarch64.tar.gz curl -LO https://github.com/kividbio/kividb/releases/latest/download/kividb-darwin-x86_64.tar.gz Each variant other than the default has its name in the file: kividb-lua-linux-x86_64.tar.gz , kividb-tls-… , kividb-full-… . The default variant is also packaged for Linux as kividb_amd64.deb / kividb_arm64.deb and kividb.x86_64.rpm / kividb.aarch64.rpm , built with nfpm from packaging/nfpm.yaml . A SHA256SUMS.txt file lists the checksum of every file in a release. curl -LO https://github.com/kividbio/kividb/releases/latest/download/kividb_amd64.deb && sudo dpkg -i kividb_amd64.deb curl -LO https://github.com/kividbio/kividb/releases/latest/download/kividb.x86_64.rpm && sudo rpm -i kividb.x86_64.rpm Configuration KiviDB is configured with command-line flags, or with a Redis-style configuration file (one directive per line, such as port 6380 or appendonly yes ). The file is read from /etc/kividb/kividb.conf if it exists; --configfile <path> names another one. A flag given on the command line wins over the same setting in the file. Run kividb --help for the full list. TLS clients connect on a separate port, --tls-port ; plain traffic stays on --port . cargo build --release --features tls ./target/release/kividb --port 6380 --tls-port 6381 --tls-cert-file cert.pem --tls-key-file key.pem redis-cli --tls -p 6381 --cacert ca.pem # ca.pem: the CA that signed cert.pem Client certificates (mutual TLS). With --tls-ca-cert-file ca.pem , clients must present a certificate signed by that CA; others are refused during the handshake. --tls-auth-clients optional accepts clients without a certificate but still refuses an invalid one, and --tls-auth-clients no does not ask for one. With redis-cli : redis-cli --tls -p 6381 --cacert ca.pem --cert client.pem --key client.key . Clients must use TLS on the TLS port. A plain connection to it (for example redis-cli -p 6381 without --tls ) fails the handshake, and the server logs [TLS] handshake failed . For memtier_benchmark, add --tls (and --tls-skip-verify for a self-signed certificate). The log goes to standard error, or to --logfile . docs/LOGGING.md describes the log; docs/ERRORS.md explains the warnings, errors and error replies, and what to do about each. When it starts, a release build of KiviDB makes one HTTPS request to https://github.com/kividbio/kividb/releases/latest , the same page you would open to find the newest release. GitHub answers with a redirect to that release's tag; if it is newer than the running build, KiviDB prints a short notice with the link before the startup banner. Nothing is sent but the request itself, with a User-Agent of kividb/<version> : no host name, configuration, keys, data or identifier. GitHub sees the request's source IP address, as any web server would. Startup waits at most 1.5 seconds for the reply; a failure is logged at debug level only and never affects clients. Only a version-shaped tag is accepted from the reply, and nothing else from it is printed. Any one of these turns it off: It is also never made by a debug build or when the CI environment variable is set. --update-check-url points it at another https:// address, such as a mirror inside a closed network. docs/UPDATE_CHECK.md has the details.
